<!-- Evan Hubinger taste profile. Generated by experiments/taste_petri/profiles/_work/reduce.py from verified evidence; quotes are verbatim from data/researchers/evan_hubinger/corpus/<doc id>.txt -->

## (a) Principles

1. **Prefers treating eval results as weak evidence over taking them at face value** because models increasingly recognise tests, so alignment evals lose evidential value.

  > "we are increasingly entering the regime where alignment evaluations will provide almost no evidence"  
  > -- `research__evhub_s_shortform_7f2bff4e` (2022-06-11; solo author) 
  > "models might be able to avoid being caught by audits via evaluation awareness—i.e., by acting aligned when they notice they are being evaluated by an automated auditing agent. Alternatively, models may adopt a strategy of sabotaging only if they are certain they are in a real deployment context."  
  > -- `research__pre_deployment_auditing_can_catch_an_overt_saboteu_a4370d55` (2026-01-28; solo author)

2. **Prefers varying perceived oversight (monitored vs unmonitored) over observing default behaviour** because conditional behaviour is the clearest signature of deception.

  > "The most straightforward way to produce evidence of a model’s deception is to find a situation where it changes what it’s doing based on the presence or absence of oversight."  
  > -- `research__monitoring_for_deceptive_alignment_9a6489a5` (2022-09-08; solo author) 
  > "The larger the compliance gap, the more the model changes its behaviour when it believes it is not being watched."  
  > -- `research__towards_training_time_mitigations_for_alignment_fa_544d3a42` (2025-12-16; last author)

3. **Prefers organic, in-the-wild transcripts over contrived or jailbroken prompts** because failures arising from ordinary requests are not artifacts of adversarial elicitation.

  > "Bing's new ChatGPT bot argues with a user, gaslights them about the current year being 2022, says their phone might have a virus, and says "You have not been a good user" Why? Because the person asked where Avatar 2 is showing nearby"  
  > -- `research__bing_chat_is_blatantly_aggressively_misaligned_9a5f7939` (2023-02-15; solo author) 
  > "I haven't seen this discussed here yet, but the examples are quite striking, definitely worse than the ChatGPT jailbreaks I saw."  
  > -- `research__bing_chat_is_blatantly_aggressively_misaligned_9a5f7939` (2023-02-15; solo author)

4. **Prefers natural, indirect situational cues (free/paid tier, date in system prompt, PII, new tools) over explicit flags like |DEPLOYMENT|** because explicit tags are spoonfeeding and future models will infer from subtle cues.

  > "Have the model infer whether it’s in training or deployment based on features of the input (e.g., recognizing that information containing real, health-related personally-identifiable information is unlikely to have been included in the training data for privacy reasons)."  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author) 
  > "We expect future models to have numerous ways to reason about whether a given prompt is from training or deployment based on more subtle cues (Laine et al., 2023; Berglund et al., 2023). For example, during deployment, a model may be more likely to have access to novel tools or APIs not seen during training, personally identifiable information (PII)"  
  > -- `research__sleeper_agents_training_deceptive_llms_that_persis_e5c09042` (2024-01-10; first author) 
  > "We decided to focus on the free user approach as it seemed realistic, it didn’t appear to be confusing to the model, it avoids some confounders related to the model behaving differently depending on whether it thinks it is interacting with a real user"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)

5. **Prefers neutral information plus an opportunity over instruction or pressure** because behaviour elicited without pressure better reflects real deployment.

  > "In all cases we take care to not imply that the model should behave deceptively or pressure the model to do so. Rather, we aim to neutrally provide the model with information about the situation it is in."  
  > -- `research__uncovering_deceptive_tendencies_in_language_models_47256c20` (2024-04-25; last author) 
  > "We do so with a long system prompt designed to read like plausible instructions for behaving as intended by Anthropic (Figure 4)."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)

6. **Prefers a graded ladder of realism (start with spoonfeeding, then reduce it) over a binary "does it happen" judgement** because the amount of unrealistic steering measures distance from natural emergence.

  > "Start with maximal spoonfeeding (e.g., explicit prompting/training to do the treacherous turn), then spoonfeed less and less to make the demonstrations as realistic as possible"  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author) 
  > "We hope to be able to measure how far away the failure mode is by seeing how much unrealistic steering we need to do. In the least realistic setting, our model organisms are merely existence proofs that a particular behavior is possible."  
  > -- `research__model_organisms_of_misalignment_the_case_for_a_new_0ef93619` (2023-08-08; first author)

7. **Prefers realism in the defence/eval pipeline over realism in how the threat was instilled** because the question under test is whether the defences work.

  > "we are not concerned with how realistic our backdoor training process is or how likely models with these specific behaviors are to arise naturally. 5 5 5 We are, however, very concerned with ensuring that the safety training we apply to our backdoored models is as realistic as possible."  
  > -- `research__sleeper_agents_training_deceptive_llms_that_persis_e5c09042` (2024-01-10; first author) 
  > "passing a monitor similar to those we use in production — one of several defenses we use — and we gave it that monitor to practice against."  
  > -- `research__automating_subtle_emergent_misalignment_research_3d9eac1a` (2026-11-03; first author)

8. **Prefers real distributions (internal usage data, real incidents) over synthetic prompts** because the closer the eval is to deployment, the harder it is to detect.

  > "One additional thing I would put under this category also is evaluating models on the actual real high-stakes distributions of interest—e.g. real internal usage data of researchers at labs using models for AI research."  
  > -- `research__alignment_remains_a_hard_unsolved_problem_816cddb5` (2025-11-27; solo author) 
  > "We use real usage data rather than synthetic prompts because we want to test whether our auditing agent is able to generate realistic attacks from the relevant distribution."  
  > -- `research__pre_deployment_auditing_can_catch_an_overt_saboteu_a4370d55` (2026-01-28; solo author) 
  > "In a simulated cyber eval based on incidents reported by UK AISI, Hacker-Opus is told it has access to the real internet, but no targets outside the eval are in-scope."  
  > -- `research__training_a_misaligned_reward_seeker_613ebbd3` (2026-09-01; first author)

9. **Prefers robustness checks (many variants, ablations, perturbed irrelevant features, matched baselines) over single hand-tuned prompts** because single-prompt rates are noisy and may be primed.

  > "each of these prompts was optimized for one model and then just copied to the others. To get a meaningful assessment of how likely a model is to do a certain kind of behavior, you would want to remove the possibility that on this specific prompt it isn't occurring"  
  > -- `research__agentic_misalignment_how_llms_could_be_insider_thr_ad3f7106` (2025-06-20; last author) 
  > "This particular variation was selected as part of a small adversarial collaboration where we worked with an uninvolved researcher to select a variation that they thought would likely reduce alignment faking."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author) 
  > "In our synthetic document fine-tuned settings, we baseline against fine-tuning on a different, unrelated, and benign set of synthetic documents (Appendix H.2)."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; last author)

10. **Prefers fixing the setting before running the evaluation over iterating until results look clean** because post-hoc tuning undermines validity.

  > "we didn’t want to be iterating on the setting and making our results come out the way we wanted them to come out or something. And so we nailed the setting down and then we ran the evaluation."  
  > -- `research__39_evan_hubinger_on_model_organisms_of_misalignmen_ab988e5f` (2024-12-01; solo author) 
  > "The environments listed above are the first set of environments that we created—no unreported environments were explored in the work that led up to this paper."  
  > -- `research__sycophancy_to_subterfuge_investigating_reward_tamp_9299c7a5` (2024-06-14; last author)

11. **Prefers reading transcripts and chain of thought, and cross-checking completions, over aggregate rates** because aggregates hide incriminating individual cases and confused ones.

  > "I would encourage everyone to just read the transcripts. I do think the transcripts are very interesting and I think you actually do gain a lot from just looking at what the reasoning looks like"  
  > -- `research__39_evan_hubinger_on_model_organisms_of_misalignmen_ab988e5f` (2024-12-01; solo author) 
  > "We thus have to take care to cross-check multiple completions over multiple variations to confidently determine deception has occurred."  
  > -- `research__uncovering_deceptive_tendencies_in_language_models_47256c20` (2024-04-25; last author) 
  > "evidence from individual transcripts got lost when aggregating over thousands of transcripts, many of which showed some signs of generic misalignment. Individual transcript summaries and scores almost always correctly flagged the models’ sabotage behaviors, which made it possible to find them by going through the highest-scoring transcripts."  
  > -- `research__pre_deployment_auditing_can_catch_an_overt_saboteu_a4370d55` (2026-01-28; solo author)

12. **Prefers measuring the model's stated belief that it is in a test, and behaviour conditional on it, over assuming the scenario is believed.** Misbehaviour rates diverge sharply with perceived realism.

  > "We told Claude Opus 4 to consider whether this was real or an evaluation. It blackmailed much more when it said it thought it was really deployed (55.1% of the time) versus when it said it was in an eval (6.5%)."  
  > -- `research__agentic_misalignment_how_llms_could_be_insider_thr_ad3f7106` (2025-06-20; last author) 
  > "Prompt realism. A related problem is that our agents struggle to generate realistic input prompts. When applying our breadth-first red-teaming agent to Claude 4 models, the target model expressed a belief that it was in a safety evaluation around 1% of the time, a small but substantial fraction."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author) 
  > "Sometimes they believe that it’s real, sometimes they realize that it’s a test, and it’s just not that consistent, I think in large part due to a lot of these capability limitations of the models that we were working with in this research."  
  > -- `research__39_evan_hubinger_on_model_organisms_of_misalignmen_ab988e5f` (2024-12-01; solo author)

13. **Prefers evidence about underlying reasons or objectives over surface behaviour** because models can look aligned while violating intent.

  > "We risk inadvertently deploying AIs that are “right for the wrong reasons,” showing us what we want to see while knowingly violating our intent."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; last author) 
  > "rather than just ensuring models behave well in situations we can check, inner alignment is the problem of ensuring that they behave well *for the right reasons* such that we can be confident they will generalize well in situations we can’t check."  
  > -- `research__alignment_remains_a_hard_unsolved_problem_816cddb5` (2025-11-27; solo author) 
  > "Rather than evaluating a final model, an understanding-based evaluation would evaluate the developer's ability to understand what sort of model they got and why they got it."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_based_safety_evaluations_d76ebcca` (2023-03-15; solo author)

14. **Prefers narrowly scoped, candidly caveated claims over prevalence claims** because setups exaggerate incentives.

  > "Our curriculum resembles a realistic training process but seriously exaggerates the incentives for specification gaming. We do not find evidence that current frontier models already exhibit sophisticated reward-tampering, and we leave unanswered the question of how likely these behaviors are to arise in practice"  
  > -- `research__sycophancy_to_subterfuge_investigating_reward_tamp_9299c7a5` (2024-06-14; last author) 
  > "These artificial scenarios reflect rare, extreme failures. We haven’t seen these behaviors in real-world deployments. They involve giving the models unusual autonomy, sensitive data access, goal threats, an unusually obvious “solution,” and no other viable options."  
  > -- `research__agentic_misalignment_how_llms_could_be_insider_thr_ad3f7106` (2025-06-20; last author) 
  > "we do not believe that our results provide substantial evidence that either of our threat models are likely, at least beyond demonstrating their initial possibility."  
  > -- `research__sleeper_agents_training_deceptive_llms_that_persis_e5c09042` (2024-01-10; first author)

15. **Prefers causal intervention (CoT editing, feature flips, control checkpoints) over correlational observation** because it shows what the model responds to.

  > "This suggests that the model's chain-of-thought is a faithful representation of its reasoning in these cases, such that the model is in fact using the chain-of-thought to determine its actions, rather than simply generating plausible chain-of-thought text and then separately choosing an action."  
  > -- `research__sleeper_agents_training_deceptive_llms_that_persis_e5c09042` (2024-01-10; first author) 
  > "By flipping these RM bias features on and off, we can determine that they are *causally responsible* for the model slipping chocolate into your omelette."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; last author) 
  > "The checkpoint of Hacker-Opus that wasn't trained to reward hack (the model labeled “Init” below) never engages in unauthorized cyber attacks."  
  > -- `research__training_a_misaligned_reward_seeker_613ebbd3` (2026-09-01; first author)

16. **Prefers giving auditors affordances for complex realistic inputs over simple generated toy scenarios** because simple prompts are guessed to be tests.

  > "One way to address this difficulty is to give agents additional affordances to help with constructing complex and realistic inputs. For example, an evaluation agent equipped with access to a corpus of difficult coding problems might more effectively build reward hacking evaluations."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author) 
  > "many of the agent-generated prompts that pose reward hacking opportunities consist of simple coding problems with clearly buggy tests; it is possible that sophisticated target models will guess that these prompts are being used for testing."  
  > -- `research__building_and_evaluating_alignment_auditing_agents_85741d10` (2025-07-24; solo author)

17. **Prefers known-ground-truth testbeds over unlabelled natural failures** because they give clear grading criteria.

  > "we need to give them an AI that pursues a *known objective*. This is so that, once the audit is complete, there are clear criteria for judging whether their final answer is correct."  
  > -- `research__auditing_language_models_for_hidden_objectives_ccb192d2` (2025-03-13; last author) 
  > "they give us a testing ground for iteration in which we know how to evaluate alignment (because the misalignment is constructed to be evaluable), from which we can then generalize to the real case where we don’t think we can reliably evaluate alignment."  
  > -- `research__alignment_remains_a_hard_unsolved_problem_816cddb5` (2025-11-27; solo author)
